verdict.best_row_rule: the row with the largest Aer f_clean (mixture) at the echo end (r = 1)
verdict.recommendation: Recommended row: **L4_all** (the best of L1-L3, ALAP), scheduled ALAP with explicit delays in the submitted circuit.  Its scheduled duration is 0.710x the as-is canary's on the fresh record (halving reached by any row: False).  Aer predicts f_clean 0.243 at the record's echo T2 and 0.028 at the transferred r = 0.174; f >= 0.1 is met at the echo end: True, at r = 0.174: False.  The break-even ratio T2*/T2_echo above which f >= 0.1 is r_crit = 0.330 (Aer, interpolated) and 0.726 (PTA bound).  This row uses the term order ['plaq0', 'hop0', 'diag', 'hop1', 'hop3', 'hop2'], a NEW coarse-step operator: it is verified here (C4, C8) but adopting it is the owner's signature (amendment), not this gate's.  Within the signed (default-order) family the best row is L1_seed_alap with Aer f_clean 0.217 at the echo end and 0.031 at r = 0.174.  The pilot's `ramw` pub on the selected patch (about 1 s of QPU, prompts/21) measures the in-circuit T2* and is read against r_crit.  Plainly: f >= 0.1 for the 2x2 step on IBM is CONDITIONAL on a T2*/T2_echo ratio above r_crit on that patch (the fez patch-1 measurements span 0.070-1.209, median 0.153, fallback 0.174); at the transferred ratio 0.174 it is not met.  The alternative is IonQ (all-to-all, gate-only f 0.216-0.303 at 2x2), with its own idle caveat: the serial-idle estimate puts Aria at 0.0506-0.0810 and Forte is not computable without published gate times -- the vendor specification of amendment 01 item 4 decides.

notes: f_proxy of the scan uses the record's MEAN cz / readout error (prompts/23 C1).  10 edges of the fresh kingston record carry IBM's uncalibrated marker 1.0, so the mean cz error is 0.0343 against a median of 0.00196 and the proxy ranks by CZ count alone; the executor admitted the top 8 by the MEDIAN-error proxy into the selection as well (the selection objective is unchanged).  The best rows came from that set.
The prompt names B1_ref00_k1 / B1_ref00_k4 for E4; the frozen set's B = 1 references are 07, 14 (skqd.krylov.references), so the first, B1_ref07, is used.
The prompt quotes the default family's B = 1 p_ref as 0.8894; the computed value is 0.889060 (the committed validation/H0P_ibm_fez.json carries the same best_r1_p).

The fractional transpilation needs FoldRzzAngle once more AFTER the level-3 optimization loop: the plugin folds right after translation, and the optimization loop then re-emits rzz(-pi/2), which the runtime's validate_rzz_pubs rejects.  The extra fold is part of the same staged pass manager.
L1_seed_alap is an executor addition: the best the SIGNED (default-order) family can do, scheduled ALAP, so that the owner can read the gain of a family change separately from the rest.

C6 first attempt: at the 4000 shots E4 prescribes, B1_ref07_k4 at r = 0.174 (25 reference hits at p_ref 0.132: reference-string f_clean 0.0553 [68 %: 0.044, 0.069] against the mixture's 0.0376 [0.033, 0.042], relative deviation 0.321 > 0.25) failed C6.  The escalation re-check found the chunk seeds strided, the chunks' raw samples distinct and the T2 override on every qubit of the patch at exactly the cell's ratio with no clipping.  The second attempt -- decided AFTER seeing the failure, and applied to all E4 cells, not only the failing one -- extends every E4 cell to 8000 shots with the same strided seed sequence (the E2 top-up mechanism).  The 4000-shot values are kept in data.C6_first_attempt_E4_4000_shots and in data.e4.aer[*][*].first_attempt_4000_shots.
